GOOD TO KNOW

Nothing changes for existing tenants: a tenant is only a proof of concept when an operator or its reseller makes it one.

FOR PLATFORM OPERATORS AND RESELLERS

Making a proof of concept: tick Proof of concept when creating a tenant, or choose Proof of concept on an existing one. Set the end date (14, 30 or 60 days, or any date), the limits (agents, supervisors, phone numbers, call minutes, SMS and WhatsApp messages, emails, AI minutes, storage), what happens at a limit (warn, or stop that use) and at the end (read only, or suspended), and the days of grace. The defaults come from the proof-of-concept template under Platform · Tenants and resellers → Proofs of concept.

Following them: the Proofs of concept list shows each one's days left and use against its limits. Extend it, convert it to a paying tenant, or end it now, each with a reason. Reminders go out 7, 3 and 1 days before the end, and notices at 80% and 100% of each limit, to the tenant's administrators and to whoever sells to it.

FOR THE TENANT

The countdown: a bar across the console and the agent desk says how many days are left and what is in use, for example 9 days left · 3 of 5 agents · 420 of 1,000 minutes. It turns amber near the end or a limit and red on the last day. Administrators see who to talk to and can choose Ask to continue.

At a limit, when set to stop: new outbound calls, campaigns and callbacks stop when minutes run out, and outbound messages and emails stop when theirs do; adding agents or numbers past their limit is refused. Inbound calls and customers' messages always get through, and no call is ever cut. Nothing is ever deleted: at the end the tenant becomes read only or suspended, and converting it brings everything back."}
